summary.headline: PVR INOX Q1 FY27 PAT of INR71 crore vs loss of INR34 crore a year ago; net cash of INR80 crore at June 30, 2026.
summary.overview: Revenue on an Ind AS 116 adjusted basis rose 12% YoY to INR1,642 crore, with EBITDA nearly doubling to INR230 crore at a 14% margin. Footfalls rose 8% to 36.6 million, with ATP at INR273 (+8%) and SPH at INR161 (+9%). The company turned net cash of INR80 crore, and management said growth can now be funded from internal cash flows. No new screens opened in Q1 because completed sites were awaiting regulatory licences; openings are expected to bunch in Q2 and Q3.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR34 crore in Q1 FY26
company describes it as debt-free; peak debt cited as INR1,450 crore
up from about 63-64%; convenience fee income +29% YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Film hire cost and F&B COGS

segments.name: Exhibition (cinemas)
segments.commentary: Footfalls 36.6 million (+8%), ATP INR273 (+8%), SPH INR161 (+9%). Premium formats are 16% of the circuit (IMAX, 4DX, ICE, ScreenX, recliners, Insignia, Director's Cut, LUXE).

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Management said ad revenue is still below its post-COVID peak and expects about a year to fully recover. Growth is expected to pick up in Q3 and Q4 with large titles; it did not give a figure.

segments.name: Alternate content and F&B
segments.commentary: Alternate content (live sports, concerts, events) ATP is about INR409; artist cost ranges from 35% to 65-70% of ticket. Food court JV with Devyani has 3 outlets open, with more in the pipeline. Web and app monetisation launched a month ago with annualised revenue of about INR2-3 crore.

guidance_outlook: Gross screen additions of 90-100 in FY27 (about 80 net after closures); Q1 had no openings and few closures are expected for the rest of the year.
FY27 capex now about INR350 crore, down from the earlier INR400 crore, including the food court JV and a higher renovation share.
Film hire cost guided at 45% to 45.5% of revenue for full-year FY27; F&B COGS expected to fall YoY.
Near-term target is a return to pre-COVID ROCE levels; no FCF target was given.
Tier 2 and Tier 3 expansion: about 300 cities identified, first opening in Muzaffarpur shortly, with asset-light and FOCO models; growth expected to accelerate from FY28.
Management expects margins of pre-COVID levels even at 27-28% occupancy.
capex_capacity: Screen count about 1,790 today, up from about 1,650 at the merger; about 120 net screens added over the last 4 years.
FY27 screen openings were held back by pending regulatory licences; openings expected to bunch in Q2 and Q3.
Closed screens in Q1 were loss-making and more than 18-20 years old; bulk of FY27 closures done in Q1.
Around 600 screens are in South India; southern concentration is about 34%, according to an analyst's estimate.
Asset-light and FOCO models are the main route for new sites; the 15 million sq ft of leased space is being offered for sublease where it is not needed.
demand_pricing: India box office grew 20% YoY in Q1 FY27 across metros, Tier 2 and Tier 3, and across languages.
North America box office was up 14% YoY at $4.8 billion in H1 2026, per management.
Hollywood share of box office is about 60% overall, about 50% for big films, and up to 80-90% for mid and smaller films.
ATP growth was driven by dynamic pricing plus premium mix; discounts are offered on Tuesdays, morning shows and front seats.

Management sees no INR500 crore-plus film so far in the year, but says mid-scale films are performing; it views the upcoming slate (Ramayana, King, Love and War, Toxic, Avengers: Doomsday, Dune: Part Three) as strong.
Management said the occupancy trend is recovering as release windows return to 8 weeks, but did not disclose a current occupancy figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are the screen closures and asset-light mix affecting the FY27 screen and capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross screen additions are still 90-100 and net additions about 80. Capex is now about INR350 crore versus INR400 crore earlier, because FOCO and capital-light demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revisit asset-light models now that it is net cash, and is more real estate monetisation planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset-light and FOCO will continue and will not limit growth of 100-120 screens a year. Capital will be deployed where needed without borrowing. Real estate monetisation is not planned at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why have footfalls stayed flat at 14-15 crore over rolling 12 months despite southern screen additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the southern skew reflects where opportunities are; 150 million admissions last year was the post-COVID high. It said occupancy is recovering and that margins at 27-28% occupancy can match pre-COVID levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 FCF target and what is the plan for surplus cash, including buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Sharma said there is no FCF target. The immediate goal is pre-COVID ROCE. Shareholder returns, including buyback, are being evaluated and will be disclosed when the Board decides.

qa_highlights.question: What are the unit economics of properties on the capital-light models?
qa_highlights.answer: Properties take 12-18 months to mature. FY24 and FY25 vintages are at margins above company level, and first-vintage performance will be shared by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did online penetration rise and what is the app/web monetisation revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Online penetration rose to about 69% on marketing and content mix. Growth will slow from here. The app/web ad product launched a month ago with annualised revenue of about INR2-3 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did film hire and COGS fall about 200 bps YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Film hire fell because Dhurandhar was in its lower-rate third and fourth weeks, and there was no mega-blockbuster to trigger bonus payouts. F&B COGS have fallen YoY for two years.

risks_watch: Release calendar: no INR500 crore-plus film so far in FY27; the slate depends on Ramayana, King, Love and War, Toxic and Hollywood tentpoles.
Licence delays pushed Q1 openings into Q2 and Q3; the 90-100 gross screen target depends on this bunching.
Advertising has not yet recovered to post-COVID levels; management expects about another year.
Online penetration growth is slowing near 70%, so convenience fee growth will depend on ATP and admits.
Capital allocation is undecided: buyback or other shareholder returns may be announced, and the company says it is evaluating all options.
Occupancy is still below pre-COVID levels; management has not disclosed a figure.
key_quotes: Q1 FY '27 was a strong start to the year.
We can now fund our growth from our own cash inflows, continue on our capital-light path and do so without the weight of leverage on our balance sheet.
So we are evaluating all options, including growth as well as allocating this capital, which is best for the long-term shareholder value creation.
Yes, it would take another maybe a year before we get to the post-COVID and go ahead of that.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, the balance sheet and the content slate, and it said so repeatedly. It was cautious on timing and capital use: advertising is expected to take about a year to recover, occupancy was not quantified, and buyback and other shareholder returns were left open with "we are evaluating all options."

adds.what: Gross screen additions of 90-100 in FY27 (about 80 net after closures); none opened in Q1, openings expected to bunch in Q2 and Q3
Tier 2/Tier 3 expansion across ~300 identified cities via asset-light and FOCO models; first opening in Muzaffarpur shortly

growth.why: Q1 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR1,642 crore with footfalls +8% and ATP +8%, and FY27 gross additions of 90-100 screens (about 5.5% of ~1,790 screens) are on track, though no openings happened in Q1 and growth is expected to accelerate only from FY28.
